jobs.description:
ABOUT HEX

Hex is growing our team of builders on a mission to make everyone a data person. Our platform solves key pain points with today’s data and analytics tooling, and empowers anyone to explore data using natural language, with or without code, on trusted context. Thousands of customers like Ramp https://hex.tech/customers/ramp/, Figma https://hex.tech/customers/figma/, Stubhub https://hex.tech/customers/stubhub/, Anthropic, and Gamma love Hex https://www.g2.com/products/hex-tech-hex/reviews for our beautiful UI, agentic superpowers, and boundless flexibility.

Hex has raised over $100M from leading investors like Sequoia, a16z, Snowflake and Amplify. With office hubs in San Francisco and New York, as well as remote team members throughout the US and UK, we’re a high-agency team that ships fast and has fun doing it. Check out our Intro to Hex video https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qAXsnrNlavk and employee handbook https://www.notion.so/hexhq/Hex-Handbook-9fff0d42860e4f70815c599e0d1664d6 to learn more about what it’s like to work at Hex.




ABOUT THE ROLE:

As Recruiting Operations Manager, you'll own the systems, processes, data, and programs that power hiring at Hex. This is a builder role.

You'll take a recruiting function that's growing fast and give it infrastructure that scales: clean data, sharp reporting, efficient workflows, and a hiring experience we're proud of. The goal isn't a process that merely holds up under load. It's a hiring system that gets measurably better every quarter, where automation handles the mechanical work so recruiters and hiring managers spend their time on judgment, relationships, and closing.

You'll be the person who turns "we should really fix this" into a durable, adopted process. You'll report to the Head of Talent and work cross-functionally with Finance, People Operations, and Data.


WHAT YOU'LL DO:

Architect the system

 - Own the recruiting tech stack end to end: ATS, sourcing, scheduling, and assessment tools, including configuration, integrations, and vendor management.

 - Design and continuously improve the hiring workflow from req approval and intake through sourcing, coordination, offer, and close, removing or automating manual steps wherever possible.

 - Make the build-versus-buy calls, and the consolidate-versus-keep calls. Decide what earns a place in the stack.

Own the data

 - Build recruiting analytics leadership actually uses to make decisions: pipeline health, funnel conversion, time-to-fill, source effectiveness, and hiring forecasts.

 - Establish and enforce data hygiene and reporting standards so the numbers can be trusted, including the unglamorous work of making sure signal gets captured on candidates we pass on, not just the ones we hire.

 - Partner with Finance and People on headcount planning, req management, and the operational link between the hiring plan and what's actually in the pipeline.

Ship AI and automation with architecture behind it

 - Identify where AI genuinely improves the funnel, build it into the workflow deliberately, and define how we'll know whether it worked.

 - Set the guardrails and build the shared, reusable set of workflows the whole team runs on, so we're not accumulating a dozen private experiments with no measurable lift.

 - Be clear and opinionated about where a human stays in the loop.

Run experiments

 - Treat hiring as a system with defined inputs and outputs. Test sourcing approaches, interview structures, and automations, and measure whether they improve quality and not just speed.

 - Lead interviewer training, structured interview rollout, and consistency programs that raise the bar and reduce bias.

 - Build the operating rhythm: dashboards, weekly reporting, QBR inputs, and real adoption of the processes you create.

Protect the candidate experience

 - Own candidate experience operationally: scheduling SLAs, communication cadences, and feedback loops, so every candidate gets a smooth, high-signal process.

 - Make sure the automation underneath still reads as human. Candidates should never be able to tell where the system ends and we begin. They should just notice that we were fast, clear, and prepared.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR:

 - 6+ years in recruiting operations, talent operations, or a closely related People Ops, BizOps, or analytics role, including experience scaling a function at a high-growth company.

 - Deep hands-on expertise with an ATS (ideally Ashby) as an admin and workflow builder, not just a user.

 - Strong analytical skills. You're comfortable owning recruiting data, building dashboards, and turning funnel metrics into clear recommendations. Comfort with SQL and BI tools is a real plus.

 - Evidence you build things. Internal tools, automations, prompt libraries, or workflow experiments you shipped because you saw the problem, not because someone assigned it.

 - A track record of turning messy, manual processes into scalable, documented, adopted workflows. Adoption is the hard part and we'll ask about it.

 - Experience implementing AI-powered recruiting automation, and a clear point of view on where it helps and where it shouldn't go.

 - Sound judgment on when to automate, when to redesign the process, and when to keep it simple.

 - Experience partnering with recruiters, hiring managers, and cross-functional stakeholders across Finance, People, and Data, including non-technical audiences.

 - Comfort with ambiguity and a bias to action. This role shapes its own playbook as the function grows.

 - Bonus: headcount planning tools, HRIS systems, and experience working alongside a data team.

 

In addition to our unique culture, Hex proudly offers a competitive total rewards package, including but not limited to, market-benched salary & equity, comprehensive health benefits, and flexible paid time off.

The salary range for this role is: $140,000 - $180,000

THE ROLE

AI is changing what's possible in growth marketing faster than most teams can keep up — and the gap between teams that embrace it and those that don't is widening fast. We're looking for a performance marketer who's building for the future, not sticking to playbooks from the past.

You'll be Hex's first dedicated performance hire. You'll take full ownership of paid-attributed S1s and pipeline ARR, with real budget from day one and room to build, test, and move fast.

This is an execution role with a systems-builder mandate. We want someone who runs structured experiments as a matter of habit, stays genuinely curious about what AI is doing to their craft, and is as energized by building the machine as by running it.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

Own paid media end-to-end

 - Drive paid strategy and execution across Google Ads, LinkedIn Ads, Meta Ads, and emerging channels — keyword and audience strategy, bid management, creative iteration, and budget pacing

 - Manage and optimize 7-8 figure annual paid budgets with rigor around CAC, pipeline influence, and LTV by segment

 - Take clear ownership of paid-attributed S1s and pipeline ARR contribution, in close partnership with Demand Gen

Build the machine

 - Build automated performance marketing systems — audience pipelines, creative testing frameworks, reporting infrastructure, and bid management — integrated into Hex's internal tools, repos, and agent harnesses

 - Use Hex's own agentic features to build and document paid marketing use cases that drive meaningful ROI — and generate solutions stories the team can use with prospects

 - Run structured experiments across landing pages, audiences, creative formats, and bidding strategies; document learnings in a way the team can compound on

Connect paid to the full funnel

 - Drive top-of-funnel paid acquisition to fuel the PLG motion — partner with Growth Product, Lifecycle, and Web to connect paid signups to self-serve activation and checkouts

 - Partner with Brand Design on creative strategy and feedback loops; bring data to every creative conversation

 - Stay ahead of emerging channels and AI-native campaign tools — and bring concrete experiments before you're asked
   
   


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

Experience

 - 5–8 years in performance marketing, with direct ownership (not just oversight) of 6– and 7-figure paid budgets

 - Hands-on experience running Google Ads, LinkedIn Ads, and Meta Ads — fluent in the nuances of each platform, not just their interfaces

 - Background at a B2B SaaS, developer tools, or data infrastructure company preferred

Skills

 - Experience building marketing automation and systems using tools like Clay, Zapier, HubSpot, and APIs

 - Familiarity with both PLG and SLG funnels and how paid strategy differs across each

 - Demonstrated use of AI tools — Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, or similar — to meaningfully automate or accelerate your work. We want specific examples.

 - Familiarity with Salesforce for CRM and pipeline attribution context (nice to have)

You might be a great fit if you…

 - Don't wait for a brief to test a hypothesis, or permission to flag a problem

 - Are as energized by building the infrastructure as by running the campaigns

 - Want to actually use the product you're marketing — and find real ways to put it to work
   
   


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

Within 12 months:

 - Paid channels have clear ownership of sourced S1s, pipeline ARR, and self-serve revenue contribution, with consistent reporting against targets

 - An automated performance marketing system is in production — audience pipelines, creative testing, and reporting infrastructure built into Hex's own tooling

 - Hex has documented, repeatable paid marketing use cases built on our own agentic platform — stories the GTM team actively uses with prospects

The on-target-earnings (base + variable) for this role is: $163,000 - $205,000.
